behavior.accepted_set_note: Stated literally: newline, carriage return, double quote, colon, backslash. The set is odd and is not rationalized into a category; no meaning is claimed for it.
behavior.arguments: dil = low byte of edi (the window reads only dil for its comparisons); the bit-test path uses the full edi after sub $0x23, so its index is (edi - 0x23) mod 64 in general
behavior.branch_order: signed-byte compares in order: > 0x5c returns 0; > 0x22 takes the bit-test path; 0x0a returns 1; 0x0d returns 1; else 0
behavior.bt_path_note: For a zero-extended byte input in 0x23..0x5c the bit-test index is byte - 0x23, so the accepted bytes on that path are 0x23, 0x3a, 0x5c. For a non-zero-extended edi the index is (edi - 0x23) mod 64; the confirmed caller sign-extends the byte into edi, so for that caller the index is exactly byte - 0x23
behavior.caller_setup: movsbl 0x0(%rbp),%r15d; mov %r15d,%edi; mov %r15d,%r14d; call 0x5430860 at 0x54309be; caller purpose beyond that is not claimed
behavior.output_shape: eax = 0 or 1 (full register: eax is zeroed first, and the 1-paths write mov $0x1,%eax or sete/setb into al after the xor)
behavior.rule: signed(dil) > 0x5c -> 0; signed(dil) > 0x22 -> bit (edi - 0x23) mod 64 of mask 0x200000000800001; dil == 0x0a -> 1; dil == 0x0d -> 1; else 0
